clue.text: Subpoenaed despite being commended for courage

definitions.meaning: summoned by name to appear in court
mentioned by name in official dispatches for bravery

explanation.surface: A witness is summoned to court even though they were decorated for bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of being named officially: in a summons or in a military dispatch.

clue.text: Questioned being put on one's mettle

explanation.surface: Someone interrogated finds the experience a test of nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute a claim and to dare someone to prove themselves are both senses of the same verb.

clue.text: The moment's come to show sex appeal!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation that the decisive time has arrived
IT is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An announcement that it's time to flaunt one's allure.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'the crucial time is here', and IT was 1920s slang for sexual magnetism.

clue.text: Arab guide and doctor take silver to Arab sultanate

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A desert guide and a physician bring silver on a trip to the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an interpreter and guide for travellers in Arabic- and Turkish-speaking lands.

clue.text: Confirms that the bulls are in?

definitions.meaning: in stock-market slang bulls and bears are opposites, so if the bulls are in, the bears are out

explanation.surface: A trader checks whether the optimistic buyers have taken over the market.
explanation.definitionFit: To corroborate a story is a phrasal-verb synonym; the second reading is a market joke about rising and falling traders.

clue.text: Set-backs do not affect Auntie

indicators.note: reading the letters from the back changes nothing, which signals a word that reads the same both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An elderly relative is unbothered by misfortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC, whose other nickname reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British nicknames for the BBC, the national broadcaster.

clue.text: Fiddle creates a noise

explanation.surface: Playing the violin badly makes a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest scheme and a loud clamour are both meanings of the same word.

clue.text: Designs are not elaborate

indicators.note: to design is to arrange anew, so the letters of 'are not' are laid out in a fresh pattern

explanation.surface: A remark that certain patterns are plain, not fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designs' looks like the subject noun but is a verb working on 'are not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate decoration is elaborate, highly embellished work.

clue.text: Be disposed to pay patient attention

definitions.meaning: to look after, as a nurse cares for a sick person

explanation.surface: A nurse is inclined to give careful care.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb means both to have a tendency and to care for, as a nurse looks after the sick.

clue.text: Spanish port I'm unable to put into beer

indicators.note: the phrase for inability is placed inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
I can't means I'm unable

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in a Spanish resort can't manage to add something to their beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a port city on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Reluctant to support the lottery recurrently

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: running back again, so the word for the lottery is read in reverse

parts.note: a lottery is a draw

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to keep funding the lottery week after week.
explanation.definitionFit: Being backward in coming forward means shy or hesitant, so the word can mean reluctant.

clue.text: A beating proves embarrassing

parts.note: a bashing is a beating

explanation.surface: A thrashing turns out to be humiliating.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone ashamed or disconcerted, so abashing means causing embarrassment.

clue.text: Flattened yobbo without assistance

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside: the word for yobbo goes around the word for help

parts.note: yobbo is British slang for a lout or hooligan
aid means assistance

explanation.surface: A thug was knocked down with nobody to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: To be knocked flat is to be laid out, as a boxer floored by a punch.

clue.text: Speculate that her toe is broken

indicators.note: the letters of 'her toe is' are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a woman has fractured her toe.
explanation.definitionFit: To form theories is to speculate or conjecture.

clue.text: Ambassador without guile, but without mercy

parts.note: HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
artless means innocent, free of guile

explanation.surface: An envoy may be naive yet also ruthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no heart lacks compassion, so the word means pitiless or cruel.

clue.text: Albert gets absorbed in wild Austrian orgy

indicators.note: the short name goes inside the jumbled letters
the letters of 'Austrian' run wild and rearrange

parts.note: Al is a short form of Albert

explanation.surface: A man named Albert is drawn into a wild Austrian party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' reads as describing the orgy but is the anagram signal; the shuffled letters give SATURNIA, which 'gets absorbed in' opens for the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnalia was a Roman winter festival of revelry, hence any riotous party or orgy.

clue.text: Become accustomed to don uniform

definitions.meaning: to put on a habit, the robe worn by a monk or nun

explanation.surface: A new recruit adjusts to wearing the regulation dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make something routine, and literally describes putting on a religious robe.

clue.text: Has to admit swindle in Sussex

indicators.note: the word 'has' opens to let in the word for a swindle

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick or swindle

explanation.surface: Someone must confess to a fraud committed in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Sussex' defines a place found there: Hastings is a seaside town in East Sussex, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings is a town on the East Sussex coast, famed for the battle of 1066.

clue.text: Rising Socialist of upright nature gets the boot

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, Britain's socialist party
moral means principled, upright

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician of high principle is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the boot' suggests dismissal, but 'the boot' is the definition: a balmoral is a laced ankle boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A balmoral is a style of laced walking boot named after the Scottish royal estate.

clue.text: Discount the inference

definitions.meaning: an amount taken off a price

explanation.surface: A shopper reasons that a price has been reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtraction from a total and a logical conclusion are both senses of the same noun.

clue.text: Do apprentices work to dish out food?

parts.note: L is a learner, so two learners are LL
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A question whether trainee cooks help serve meals.
explanation.definitionFit: To dollop is to serve out food in large shapeless spoonfuls.

clue.text: Copper and solicitor suddenly stopped working

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor in the literal sense

explanation.surface: A police officer and a lawyer abruptly downed tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'solicitor' suggest police and a lawyer; one is a chemical symbol and the other a street hawker.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine or a power supply that cuts out stalls or fails abruptly.

clue.text: Agent ordered to hold mother at the entrance

indicators.note: the jumbled letters enclose the word for mother
the letters of 'Agent' are put into a new order

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An agent is told to detain a woman at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the entrance' reads as a place, but defines a person by his post; 'ordered' shuffles to GATEN, which 'to hold' opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateman is a keeper stationed at an entrance, so the definition describes him by his post.

clue.text: No-one on land is confused

definitions.meaning: describes everyone being out on the ocean

explanation.surface: A sailor is bewildered when nobody is ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being bewildered literally describes a crew out on the ocean.

clue.text: In Madras I attempted to be continent

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: A traveller in an Indian city tries to keep their composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continent' looks like the adjective meaning self-restrained, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the Earth's great landmasses.

clue.text: Talented labour leader in Lincoln

indicators.note: the picked letter goes inside the short name

parts.note: Abe was the familiar name of US President Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word labour is taken

explanation.surface: A gifted Labour Party leader comes from the city of Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable and skilful people are described as gifted or competent.

clue.text: First Regent to enter Lebanon in order to show the flag

indicators.note: that letter goes inside the rearranged country name
the letters of the country's name are put into a fresh order
the opening letter of the word Regent is taken

explanation.surface: A regent is the first to arrive in Lebanon, flying the national colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges LEBANON and 'to enter' puts the R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bannerol is a small banner or streamer, such as one carried at a funeral.

clue.text: Primate harbours little desire

indicators.note: the word for the animal shelters the word for small inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
petite means small, little

explanation.surface: A monkey has only a small wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a craving or wish, for food or anything else.

clue.text: Old dictator gets total American backing

indicators.note: read backwards, the two words are reversed together

parts.note: all means total, the whole

explanation.surface: A former tyrant enjoys complete support from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulla was a Roman general who made himself dictator around 82 BC.
